sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Cheatham County?
sections.html:
Deeds and mortgages for property in Cheatham County are recorded at the Register of Deeds, 354 Frey Street, Suite C, in Ashland City. The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. and the phone number is (615) 792-4317. Chrissy Henderson is the Register.

The other offices a seller meets share the Frey Street address: the Trustee in Suite A at (615) 792-4298, and the Assessor of Property in Suite B at (615) 792-5371. Ashland City is the county seat, and Kingston Springs, Pegram and Pleasant View are the other incorporated places. The county government site lists these four municipalities.

sections.h2: What does the Cheatham County Register of Deeds do and not do?
sections.html:
The Register records legal instruments, mostly those that transfer title to land, and keeps the public index. Tennessee Code section 8-13-108 lists many of the duties, and other statutes add more.

  • The office cannot prepare, change or revise a deed. State law bars the staff from practicing law, so a seller or buyer should use an attorney or a title company for that step.
  • It cannot run a title search. The staff will help you see which recorded instruments might be liens, but a title company or attorney does the actual search.
  • Indexes are by name only. To look up a parcel by address, call the county Assessor at (615) 792-5371.
  • Only an original, signed and authenticated instrument can be recorded. The one copy the office will accept is a certified copy of something already recorded or filed in another government office.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record or copy documents in Cheatham County?
sections.html:
Recording fees depend on the type of document, so the office asks you to call (615) 792-4317 for a calculation before you send a deed. Copy prices are posted and are small.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax applies when a Cheatham County house sells?
sections.html:
Tennessee charges a realty transfer tax of 37 cents per $100 on every transfer of real estate, and the tax is generally based on the greater of the price paid or the value of the property. It is part of the state recordation tax under Tenn. Code Ann. 67-4-409, which also taxes recorded debt such as a deed of trust at $0.115 per $100 after the first $2,000.

The Census Bureau's median value of an owner-occupied Cheatham County home for 2020 to 2024 is $338,700. At 37 cents per $100, a sale at that price carries about $1,253 in transfer tax. A buyer's $270,000 mortgage would add about $308 in mortgage tax, since $268,000 of it is taxable. Ask the closing agent for the exact amounts and who pays each one under your contract.

sections.h2: How does county property tax fit into a Cheatham County sale?
sections.html:
The Trustee collects county property tax and the Assessor sets the value, so neither question goes to the Register. The Trustee's rule is that the owner on January 1 is responsible for that year's tax. A sale contract can shift the cost between buyer and seller, but the Trustee keeps no record of such contracts and tells anyone who buys or sells during the year to verify that the tax is paid, bill or no bill.

The 2026 bill can be paid without interest through Friday, February 26, 2027 at the Trustee's office, and banks take current-year payments through February 28, 2027. From March 1, 1.5 percent is added each month. Real property stays with the Trustee until it is a full year delinquent, then goes to the delinquent tax attorney and a Chancery Court suit between March 16 and March 31. Call (615) 792-4298 for the amount on a specific parcel.

The Trustee's office is in Suite A at 354 Frey Street, with hours of 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday and Wednesday, 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. Tuesday and Thursday, and 8 a.m. to noon Friday. Because deeds are recorded under varied spellings, the Trustee advises owners to track every parcel bought or sold in the year, and a seller should bring the bill to the closing.

sections.h2: How does the Register of Deeds connect to the county assessment?
sections.html:
The Assessor of Property, in Suite B at the same address, relies on the deeds the Register records. The Assessor's brochure says the primary tool for value is comparing what similar properties sell for, using the hundreds of sales recorded each year by the Register of Deeds. A deed you record therefore becomes a data point in a later reappraisal.

The brochure says Cheatham County is on a five year reappraisal cycle, and gives 2019 as the last reappraisal before its printing. Contact the Assessor at (615) 792-5371 for the current reappraisal year. A property owner who disagrees with a value should talk to the Assessor first, and the County Board of Equalization begins meeting in the first days of June. The board hears evidence on value, not on the amount of tax, and it cannot change the rate.

Low-income elderly and disabled owners, and disabled veterans or their surviving spouses, can apply for state Tax Relief at the Trustee's office if the home is their primary residence in the county.

Cheatham County sits in Middle Tennessee as part of the Nashville-Davidson-Murfreesboro-Franklin metropolitan area. The General Assembly created it in 1856 from parts of Davidson, Dickson, Montgomery and Robertson counties, and it was named for state legislator Edward Saunders Cheatham.

The county covers about 302 square miles of land. The Cumberland River crosses it from northwest to southeast with Ashland City on its northern bank, the Harpeth River winds through the hilly south, and Pleasant View sits just south of Interstate 24 on the northern edge. Kingston Springs sits mostly north of Interstate 40, and Pegram lies along U.S. Route 70.

The Census Bureau estimated 42,778 residents in July 2025 and 18,310 housing units. For 2020 to 2024 it reports 16,279 households, median household income of $89,852 and a mean commute of 33.5 minutes. Owners occupy 81.5 percent of homes, which is high, and median gross rent is $1,345. Builders took out 285 permits in 2025.

sections.h2: What should a Cheatham County seller prepare before the deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Bring or send the signed original deed, a clear legal description and the consideration so the tax can be figured. Get the name spelling right on every party, because the index is searched by name.

  • Confirm with the Register whether any fee applies to the deed and any release of a prior mortgage.
  • Get a payoff from the lender and a tax status from the Trustee.
  • Pay any past due county tax before the deed is recorded.
  • Ask for a certified copy, at $1.00 per page, if a lender or court needs one.

faqs.q: Where is the Cheatham County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The office is at 354 Frey Street, Suite C, Ashland City, TN 37015. It is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and the phone number is (615) 792-4317.

faqs.q: How much is the Tennessee transfer tax in Cheatham County?
faqs.a: The realty transfer tax is $0.37 per $100 of the transfer. A $338,700 sale, the Census median for Cheatham County, would owe about $1,253.

faqs.q: Can the Cheatham County Register of Deeds write my deed?
faqs.a: No. The office cannot prepare, change or revise a deed because Tennessee prohibits the staff from practicing law. Use an attorney or title company.

faqs.q: Can I search Cheatham County deed records by address?
faqs.a: Not at the Register's office, since indexes are by name. Call the Cheatham County Assessor of Property at (615) 792-5371 to look up a parcel by address.

faqs.q: How much does a certified copy cost in Cheatham County?
faqs.a: A certified copy costs $1.00 per page. Plain copies are $0.15 per page, and large plat copies are $5.00 per page.
